about: Evidence recommendations for the national technology security policies of Annex E of the UAE Information Assurance Standard v2.1, as extra rows of the UAE IA library (rows E1-*, E2-* and E3-* of uae_ia_annex_e_rows.json): E1 National Cloud Security Policy (Table 10), E2 National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence (Table 11) and E3 National IoT Security Policy (Table 12). Authored for this library: the annex names no evidence. Every item is grounded in the row's own statements and bullets, and 'covers' lists the numbered obligations (the row's `obligations`, 1-based) it helps to evidence; every obligation of every row is covered by at least one item. build_uae_ia_annex_e_rows.py merges this file into the generated rows as evidence_requirements {name, description, filetype} and drops 'covers'; collection_frequency is kept where the item is event-driven or continuous (the seeder reads it from dict entries and otherwise defaults to annually).

E1-2.1.1.name: Approved cloud security policy
E1-2.1.1.description: Policy document approved by management that sets out the entity's cloud security requirements, with its owner, version and approval date.

E1-2.1.1.name: Cloud security policy review record
E1-2.1.1.description: Record of the periodic review of the cloud security policy, showing who reviewed it, when, and what was changed or confirmed.

E1-2.1.1.name: Cloud usage analysis
E1-2.1.1.description: Analysis of what the entity keeps and runs in the cloud: the information and application assets held, the multi-tenant virtualized services used, the users and the privileged administrators.

E1-2.1.1.name: Provider access and data location analysis
E1-2.1.1.description: Analysis of the access the cloud service provider has to the entity's information and of the countries where the provider is based and may store its data, even temporarily.

E1-2.1.2.name: Cloud risk register
E1-2.1.2.description: Register of the security and privacy risks of the cloud environment, with the owner, rating and treatment status of each.

E1-2.1.2.name: Cloud risk assessment
E1-2.1.2.description: Assessment that identifies and rates the security and privacy risks of the cloud environment, with the method used and the date performed.

E1-2.1.2.name: Cloud risk treatment plan
E1-2.1.2.description: Plan recording the mitigation chosen for each cloud risk, with its owner, due date and progress.

E1-2.1.2.name: Cloud risk communication record
E1-2.1.2.description: Evidence that cloud risks were communicated to management and other stakeholders, such as committee minutes or briefing notes.

E1-2.1.3.name: Cloud provider contract personnel clauses
E1-2.1.3.description: Extracts of the executed contracts with each cloud service provider (CSP) showing clauses for background screening of its personnel, regular user awareness and training, disciplinary measures and an orderly exit, including contract termination.

E1-2.1.3.name: Shared responsibility matrix
E1-2.1.3.description: Matrix that allocates each security responsibility to the entity or to the CSP and shows how duties are segregated between them.

E1-2.1.3.name: CSP contract clause checklist
E1-2.1.3.description: Checklist completed for each CSP contract confirming it includes personnel screening, a responsibilities matrix with segregation of duties, awareness and training, a disciplinary measure and an orderly exit.

E1-2.1.4.name: CSP onboarding risk assessment
E1-2.1.4.description: Risk assessment completed before a CSP is onboarded, showing the risks identified and the decision taken.

E1-2.1.4.name: Subcontracting risk assessment
E1-2.1.4.description: Assessment of the risks created when a CSP relies on other providers to deliver the service, with the approval or refusal of each one.

E1-2.1.4.name: CSP risk treatment record

E1-2.1.4.name: Approved CSP register

E1-2.1.5.name: Independent assurance reports from the CSP
E1-2.1.5.description: Latest independent third-party test results and audit reports for the CSP service, as obtained from the provider.

E1-2.1.5.name: Review of CSP assurance reports
E1-2.1.5.description: Record of the entity's review of the provider's independent reports, noting scope, findings and any gaps for follow-up.

E1-2.1.5.name: CSP security certifications
E1-2.1.5.description: Certificates held by the CSP that cover the service in use, with their scope and expiry dates.

E1-2.1.5.name: Assurance gap follow-up actions
E1-2.1.5.description: Actions raised with the CSP for gaps found in its independent assurance, with owner and status.

E1-2.2.1.name: CSP due diligence questionnaire
E1-2.2.1.description: Completed security questionnaire for the CSP, answered before onboarding, covering its security posture and compliance.

E1-2.2.1.name: CSP due diligence assessment report
E1-2.2.1.description: Report of the pre-onboarding assessment of the CSP's security posture and compliance, with findings and the onboarding decision.

E1-2.2.1.name: Onboarding approval record

E1-2.2.1.name: Non-disclosure agreement with the CSP

E1-2.2.2.name: Executed CSP contract

E1-2.2.2.name: Service level agreement with availability terms
E1-2.2.2.description: Service level agreement that sets the availability commitments agreed for the service.

E1-2.2.2.name: Sovereignty, data ownership and location clauses

E1-2.2.2.name: Incident, change and audit rights clauses
E1-2.2.2.description: Contract clauses covering how incidents are notified to the entity, change management and the entity's right to audit the CSP.

E1-2.2.2.name: Exit, vendor lock-in and dispute clauses
E1-2.2.2.description: Contract clauses on service exit, minimizing vendor lock-in and the arbitration and dispute resolution mechanism.

E1-2.3.1.name: Data classification policy

E1-2.3.1.name: Cloud data handling procedure

E1-2.3.1.description: Analysis of the regulatory, statutory and supply chain obligations that apply to data wherever it resides in the cloud or is shared with third parties.

E1-2.3.1.name: Pre-migration data classification record

E1-2.3.1.name: National cloud classification level mapping

E1-2.3.2.name: Encryption policy
E1-2.3.2.description: Approved policy setting when and how encryption protects sensitive data in storage and in transmission, tied to the legal and regulatory obligations that apply.

E1-2.3.2.description: Screenshots of the encryption settings for cloud storage and for data in transit.

E1-2.3.2.name: Cloud encryption key management procedure

E1-2.3.2.name: Hold your own key risk assessment

E1-2.3.2.name: Key custody and independence evidence

E1-2.4.1.name: CSP jurisdiction and data location assessment

E1-2.4.1.name: Cloud data location register

E1-2.4.1.name: Classified data hosting matrix
E1-2.4.1.description: Matrix of each classification level with the cloud environment it requires, Partial Sovereign Cloud or Sovereign Cloud, and the environment actually used.

E1-2.5.1.name: Interoperability needs evaluation

E1-2.5.2.name: CSP contract data portability clauses

E1-2.5.2.name: CSP data portability commitment

E1-2.5.2.name: Data export test result

E1-2.6.1.name: CSP change management evidence

E1-2.6.2.name: Independent data center security reports

E1-2.6.3.name: Cloud asset inventory

E3-2.2.1.name: IoT data use and rights contract terms
E3-2.2.1.description: Contract terms that give clear and transparent information on how data is used, by whom and for what purposes for each IoT device and service, and let the entity exercise its rights over its data, such as access, erasure, rectification and portability.

E3-2.2.1.name: IoT data protection and access restriction evidence
E3-2.2.1.description: Evidence that the confidentiality, integrity and availability of IoT data, including personally identifiable information (PII), is protected and that access to the physical and digital locations of data is restricted to authorized individuals.

E3-2.2.1.name: CSP contract clauses for IoT data
E3-2.2.1.description: Executed contracts with cloud service providers (CSPs) that include non-disclosure agreements, service level agreements, and security, privacy, sovereignty, availability, incident notification, service exit, change management and right to audit requirements.

E3-2.2.1.name: Data minimization and collection evidence
E3-2.2.1.description: Evidence that the collection of sensitive data is avoided and the data collected and retained is minimized, such as data collection justifications and retention limits.

E3-2.2.2.name: IoT encryption policy and procedures
E3-2.2.2.description: Policy and procedures that govern the encryption protocols used for IoT data held in storage and sent between systems, with the legal and regulatory obligations they respond to.

E3-2.2.2.name: IoT encryption configuration evidence
E3-2.2.2.description: Screenshots of the encryption settings applied to IoT data at rest and while it moves between systems.

E3-2.2.2.name: Key hierarchy certificate chain
E3-2.2.2.description: Certificate chain extract showing the root private key at the top of the key hierarchy and the keys issued beneath it.

E3-2.2.2.name: Root private key protection evidence
E3-2.2.2.description: Evidence of how the root private key is held and its use controlled, such as its storage location and access list.

E3-2.2.3.name: Session management settings
E3-2.2.3.description: Settings showing active sessions are unique, non-essential sessions are timed out and invalidated, and sessions expire after a fixed time of inactivity.

E3-2.2.3.name: Session token strength test result
E3-2.2.3.description: Result of a test showing session tokens are unique, cannot be predicted or shared and have a minimum level of entropy.

E3-2.2.3.name: IoT communication protocol specification
E3-2.2.3.description: Specification of the communication protocols between IoT systems, showing encrypted channels, integrity protection and authenticated connections.

E3-2.2.3.name: Encrypted channel verification results
E3-2.2.3.description: Scan or capture results showing connections between IoT systems use encrypted and authenticated channels.

E3-2.2.3.name: Approved encryption techniques list
E3-2.2.3.description: List of the encryption techniques used to protect data within IoT systems and their underlying infrastructure, with evidence that each is proven.

E3-2.3.1.name: IoT access rights listing
E3-2.3.1.description: List of the identities with access to IoT resources, each uniquely identified, with the privileges granted and the person accountable.

E3-2.3.1.name: IoT authentication and MFA settings
E3-2.3.1.description: Screenshots of the authentication settings for IoT systems, including multi-factor authentication.

E3-2.3.1.name: IoT credential storage and hard-coding checks
E3-2.3.1.description: Results of checks showing credentials are stored securely and that hard-coded credentials are not present in IoT software or devices.

E3-2.3.1.name: IoT access review results
E3-2.3.1.description: Results of the regular review of permissions to IoT resources, with the compensating controls put in place where needed.

E3-2.3.1.name: IoT password rules configuration
E3-2.3.1.description: Configured password complexity and periodic update requirements for IoT systems.

E3-2.3.2.name: IoT location access control list
E3-2.3.2.description: List of the people authorized to enter IoT environments, buildings, locations and rooms.

E3-2.3.2.name: Physical access control evidence
E3-2.3.2.description: Screenshots or photographs of the controls on physical access to IoT locations, such as badge reader settings or locks.

E3-2.3.2.name: Physical access monitoring records
E3-2.3.2.description: Access records, such as door logs or visitor logs, showing physical access to IoT locations is monitored.

E3-2.4.1.name: IoT incident response procedure
E3-2.4.1.description: Procedure for identifying, responding to, containing and recovering from IoT incidents, with the incident response plan, reporting, classification and recovery steps.

E3-2.4.1.name: IoT incident records
E3-2.4.1.description: Records of IoT incidents showing how each was reported, classified and recovered from.

E3-2.4.1.name: Post-incident analysis report
E3-2.4.1.description: Report of the post-incident analysis of an IoT incident, with the lessons learned.

E3-2.4.1.name: Incident evidence collection records
E3-2.4.1.description: Records of the evidence collected during IoT incidents, with who collected it and when.

E3-2.4.1.name: Threat intelligence resourcing and outputs
E3-2.4.1.description: Allocation of resources to monitor and track security threats using threat intelligence, with examples of the threat information tracked.

E3-2.5.1.name: IoT backup schedule and settings
E3-2.5.1.description: Schedule and settings for the periodic backup of user and configuration data from IoT systems.

E3-2.5.1.name: IoT backup job logs
E3-2.5.1.description: Backup logs showing the periodic backups of user and configuration data completed.

E3-2.5.1.name: IoT backup restoration test results
E3-2.5.1.description: Outcome of a trial restoration of IoT backups, with the time taken and any problems met.

E3-2.5.2.name: IoT continuity plan
E3-2.5.2.description: Approved plan that sets out how the entity continues IoT services through a disruption.

E3-2.5.2.name: IoT response and recovery procedures
E3-2.5.2.description: Procedures that detail how the entity manages disruptions to IoT services, including response and recovery.

E3-2.5.2.name: IoT continuity test results
E3-2.5.2.description: Results of the periodic test of the IoT continuity plans, with the actions raised.

E3-2.6.1.name: IoT asset inventory
E3-2.6.1.description: Inventory of IoT systems, including devices, software and firmware, with owner and location.

E3-2.6.1.name: IoT device handling procedure
E3-2.6.1.description: Procedure for the appropriate handling of IoT devices.

E3-2.6.1.name: IoT device maintenance records
E3-2.6.1.description: Records of the maintenance performed on IoT devices, with dates and who carried it out.

E3-2.6.1.name: IoT device disposal records
E3-2.6.1.description: Records showing IoT devices were properly disposed of, with the date and method.

E3-2.6.2.name: IoT component authentication and encryption settings
E3-2.6.2.description: Settings for IoT applications, middleware, APIs and devices showing secure authentication and information exchange over encrypted channels.

E3-2.6.2.name: IoT application security architecture
E3-2.6.2.description: Architecture document showing the end-to-end security controls and availability aspects across the IoT solution.

E3-2.6.2.name: Trusted service layer access control rules
E3-2.6.2.description: Export of the access control rules enforced on the trusted service layer.

E3-2.6.2.name: Dedicated IoT gateway evidence
E3-2.6.2.description: Evidence that a secure and dedicated gateway is used for normalizing and handling data within IoT networks, such as its network placement and settings.

E3-2.6.3.name: IoT device installation and setup baseline
E3-2.6.3.description: Baseline for installing and setting up IoT devices and sensors so unauthorized access is prevented, with a sample of devices checked against it.

E3-2.6.3.name: Remote management evidence
E3-2.6.3.description: Screenshots showing IoT devices are managed remotely over encrypted channels and that security event recording is enabled.

E3-2.6.3.name: IoT device management strategy
E3-2.6.3.description: Documented strategy for the periodic update and maintenance of IoT devices.

E3-2.6.3.name: IoT patch and update records
E3-2.6.3.description: Records of security patches from authentic sources, their compatibility testing and the risk and impact assessment made before each update was deployed.

E3-2.6.3.name: End-of-life device compensating measures
E3-2.6.3.description: Compensatory measures applied to IoT devices that have reached end-of-life, with the devices covered.

E3-2.7.1.name: IoT network architecture diagram
E3-2.7.1.description: Diagram showing IoT networks segregated from the corporate network with micro-segmentation, a separate management network and the routing networks they cross.

E3-2.7.1.name: Segmentation and traffic restriction rules
E3-2.7.1.description: Firewall or segmentation rules that restrict and control information exchange and infrastructure management of IoT devices and applications.

E3-2.7.1.name: Secure ports and protocols settings
E3-2.7.1.description: Settings showing IoT networks use secure ports and protocols with authentication and encryption enabled.

E3-2.7.1.name: Unused and default service scan results
E3-2.7.1.description: Scan results showing unused and default network services, protocols and ports are disabled.

E3-2.7.1.name: Consumer IoT device cryptography evidence
E3-2.7.1.description: Evidence that consumer IoT devices use best practice cryptography for secure communications.

E3-2.8.1.name: IoT logging settings
E3-2.8.1.description: Screenshots of the logging settings that show which events are recorded for IoT devices, systems and applications.

E3-2.8.1.name: Authentication and access event log extracts
E3-2.8.1.description: Extracts of IoT logs showing user logins, logouts, unsuccessful authentication, connection and authorization attempts, and changes in access privileges.

E3-2.8.1.name: Data and operation event log extracts
E3-2.8.1.description: Extracts of IoT logs showing access to sensitive data, import and export from removable media, creation, modification and deletion of data, impactful operations and remote operations.

E3-2.8.1.name: Update failure and physical access event logs
E3-2.8.1.description: Logs of security update failures and, where possible, physical access attempts and emergency access attempts.

E3-2.8.1.name: Log storage, protection and analysis records
E3-2.8.1.description: Evidence that IoT logs are stored, protected from tampering and analyzed, such as retention settings, access restrictions and analysis reports.
